changes_made.explanation: Changed answer from Yes to No because this paper focuses on word alignment (an NLP analysis task) rather than natural language generation tasks. Removed 'Machine Translation' as the paper evaluates word alignment models, not MT systems. Normalized model names and removed duplicate dataset entry.
Normalized metric names to standard capitalization and removed duplicates. These metrics are correctly used for evaluating word alignment quality.
No LLMs were used as evaluators in this paper. The paper mentions using pre-trained language models (BERT, XLM-R) as backbone models for word alignment, but not as evaluators.
No human evaluation was conducted in this paper. The evaluation relies entirely on benchmark datasets with gold-standard alignments.

overall_notes: This paper focuses on word alignment as a standalone NLP task, not on NLG evaluation. While word alignment has applications in machine translation, the paper itself does not evaluate NLG systems or generated text. The extraction quality was generally good, but incorrectly categorized this as an NLG paper when it's primarily about an NLP analysis task.
